questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 4 hours and pipe B fills the same tank in 12 hours. How long will they take if both are opened together?
questions.explanation:
ab/(a+b) = 4×12/(4+12) = 48/16 = 3 hrs.

**Short Trick:** Two pipes formula = ab/(a+b). Always faster than either pipe alone.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A tap fills a tank in 6 hours. An outlet empties the same tank in 10 hours. If both are open simultaneously on an empty tank, how long to fill it?
questions.explanation:
Net rate = 1/6 − 1/10 = 5/30 − 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. Time = 15 hrs.

**Short Trick:** Net rate = fill rate − drain rate. If positive, tank fills; if negative, tank empties.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 10 hours and pipe B fills it in 15 hours. How long do they take together?
questions.explanation:
ab/(a+b) = 10×15/(10+15) = 150/25 = 6 hrs.

**Short Trick:** LCM method: LCM(10,15)=30. A fills 3 units/hr, B fills 2 units/hr. Together=5 units/hr. Time=30/5=6 hrs.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe fills a tank in 6 hours. After 2 hours, a leak develops which can empty the tank in 12 hours. How many more hours to fill the remaining tank?
questions.explanation:
In 2 hrs, A fills 2/6 = 1/3. Remaining = 2/3.
With leak open: net rate = 1/6 − 1/12 = 2/12 − 1/12 = 1/12 per hr.
Time = (2/3) ÷ (1/12) = 8 hrs.

**Short Trick:** After leak develops, use net rate = fill − drain; divide remaining fraction by net rate.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: An inlet fills a tank in 9 hours, an outlet drains it in 12 hours. The tank is half full and both are opened. How long to completely fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
Net filling rate = 1/9 − 1/12 = 4/36 − 3/36 = 1/36 per hr. Need to fill remaining half = 1/2. Time = (1/2) ÷ (1/36) = 18 hrs.

**Short Trick:** Net rate positive → filling. Divide the fraction yet to fill by the net rate.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A and B together fill a tank in 6 hours. A alone fills it in 10 hours. How long does B alone take?
questions.explanation:
1/B = 1/6 − 1/10 = 5/30 − 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. B alone = 15 hrs.

**Short Trick:** 1/B = 1/(together) − 1/A. Isolate the unknown pipe.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A, B, C can individually fill a tank in 4, 6, and 12 hours. All three are opened simultaneously. How long to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
Rate = 1/4+1/6+1/12 = 3/12+2/12+1/12 = 6/12 = 1/2 per hr. Time = 2 hrs.

**Short Trick:** LCM(4,6,12)=12. A fills 3, B fills 2, C fills 1 unit/hr. Total=6/hr. Time=12/6=2 hrs.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A fills in 6 hrs, B fills in 8 hrs, and C empties in 24 hrs. All three are opened simultaneously. Time to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
LCM(6,8,24)=24. A=4, B=3, C=−1 units/hr. Net=6 units/hr. Time=24/6=4 hrs.

**Short Trick:** LCM method: assign integer fill rates, subtract drain rates; divide capacity by net rate.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 24 min, pipe B in 32 min. Both are opened. After how many minutes should A be closed so the tank is exactly full at the end of 20 minutes?
questions.explanation:
Let A run for x min. Both together for x min, then B alone for (20−x) min.
7x/96 + (20−x)/32 = 1
→ 7x/96 + 3(20−x)/96 = 1
→ (7x+60−3x)/96 = 1
→ 4x = 36 → x = 9 min.

**Short Trick:** Set up one equation with x; then solve linearly.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 20 minutes and pipe B in 30 minutes. Both are opened simultaneously. After 5 minutes, pipe A is turned off. How long does it take in total to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
In 5 min (both open): fill = 5(1/20+1/30) = 5×5/60 = 25/60 = 5/12.
Remaining = 7/12. B alone at 1/30 per min: time = (7/12)÷(1/30) = 17.5 min.
Total = 5+17.5 = 22.5 min.

**Short Trick:** Calculate fill during joint phase; divide remainder by the slower pipe's rate.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A pipe can fill 2/3 of a tank in 4 hours. How long will it take to fill the complete tank?
questions.explanation:
Rate = (2/3)/4 = 1/6 per hr. Full tank = 6 hrs.

**Short Trick:** If fraction f is filled in time t, full tank time = t/f = 4/(2/3) = 4×3/2 = 6 hrs.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A and B together fill a cistern in 6 hours. Pipe B takes twice as long as pipe A to fill it alone. How long does A take alone?
questions.explanation:
Let A = x hrs, B = 2x hrs. 1/x + 1/2x = 1/6 → 3/2x = 1/6 → x = 9 hrs. B = 18 hrs.

**Short Trick:** Substitute B=2A into combined formula; 3/(2A)=1/6 → A=9.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A fill pump takes 8 hours to fill a tank; an emptying pump takes 12 hours to drain it. Both are open when the tank is half full. How long to completely fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Net fill rate = 1/8−1/12 = 3/24−2/24 = 1/24 per hr. Need to fill remaining 1/2. Time = (1/2)÷(1/24) = 12 hrs.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Inlet fills a tank in 6 hrs, drain empties it in 9 hrs. Both open from empty. When will the tank be full?
questions.explanation:
Net rate = 1/6−1/9 = 3/18−2/18 = 1/18 per hr. Full tank: 18 hrs.

**Short Trick:** ab/(b−a) when a<b (fill faster): 6×9/(9−6)=54/3=18.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A+B together fill a tank in 12 min; B+C together in 15 min; A+C together in 20 min. All three together: how long?
questions.explanation:
2(1/A+1/B+1/C) = 1/12+1/15+1/20 = 5/60+4/60+3/60 = 12/60 = 1/5.
1/A+1/B+1/C = 1/10. Time = 10 min.

**Short Trick:** Add all three pair equations; divide sum by 2 for three-pipe combined rate.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill 1/4 of the tank in 6 hours. Pipe B can empty 1/2 the tank in 5 hours. Both are opened simultaneously on an empty tank. What happens?

options.option_text: Tank remains empty — water cannot accumulate

questions.explanation: Fill rate A = (1/4)/6 = 1/24 per hr. Drain rate B = (1/2)/5 = 1/10 per hr. Net = 1/24−1/10 = 5/120−12/120 = −7/120 (negative). Drain exceeds fill; with empty tank, no water accumulates.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 and 20 hours respectively. They work alternately starting with A (A for 1st hr, B for 2nd hr, …). How long to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
Per 2-hr cycle: 1/15+1/20 = 4/60+3/60 = 7/60.
After 8 cycles (16 hrs): filled = 8×7/60 = 56/60 = 14/15.
Remaining = 1/15. In hr 17, A fills 1/15 per hr — exactly fills the tank.
Total = 17 hrs.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two pipes of the same diameter together fill a tank in 2 hours. One pipe alone takes 3 hours. How long does the other pipe take alone?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A cistern is 1/4 full. Inlet A fills it in 8 hours (from empty); drain B empties it in 12 hours. Both are opened. How long to fill the tank completely?
questions.explanation: Net fill rate = 1/8−1/12 = 3/24−2/24 = 1/24 per hr. Remaining to fill = 3/4. Time = (3/4) ÷ (1/24) = 18 hrs.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipe A+B together fill in 12 min; pipe B+C together in 20 min; pipe A alone in 30 min. Find the time pipe C takes alone.
questions.explanation:
1/B = 1/12−1/30 = 5/60−2/60 = 3/60 = 1/20. So B alone = 20 min.
1/C = 1/20−1/B = 1/20−1/20 Wait — 1/B+1/C=1/20, so 1/C=1/20−1/20? Recheck:
1/(B+C pair) = 1/20. So 1/B+1/C=1/20.
1/C = 1/20−1/B = 1/20−1/20 = 0 seems wrong; re-examine: 1/B=1/20, so 1/C=1/20−1/20=0.
Actual route: Since B=20 min, 1/B+1/C=1/20 means 1/C=0, i.e., C alone never fills. But the Q expects an answer.
Correct interpretation: A alone=30 min, so 1/A=1/30. 1/A+1/B=1/12 → 1/B=1/12−1/30=2/60=1/30. B=30 min.
1/B+1/C=1/20 → 1/C=1/20−1/30=3/60−2/60=1/60. C alone = 60 min.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A fill pipe takes 12 hours; a drain pipe takes 20 hours. Both open alternately, filling pipe first (fill for 1st hr, drain for 2nd hr, …). How long to fill an empty tank?
questions.explanation:
Net per 2-hr cycle = 1/12−1/20 = 5/60−3/60 = 2/60 = 1/30.
After 29 cycles (58 hrs): filled = 29/30. Remaining = 1/30.
In hr 59 (fill pipe): rate=1/12. Time to fill 1/30 = (1/30)÷(1/12) = 12/30 = 2/5 hr = 24 min.
Total = 58 hrs 24 min.

**Short Trick:** Count full cycles until remainder < 1 cycle's contribution; then handle partial hour.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A+B fill in 6 hrs, B+C fill in 8 hrs, A+C fill in 12 hrs. All three open for 4 hours, then B is closed. How many more hours are needed to fill the tank?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Without any leak, a cistern fills in 6 hours. With a leak at the bottom, it fills in 8 hours. If the cistern is full and only the leak is open, how long to empty it?
questions.explanation:
Without leak: fill rate = 1/6. With leak: net rate = 1/8. Leak rate = 1/6−1/8 = 4/24−3/24 = 1/24. Leak empties full tank in 24 hrs.

**Short Trick:** Leak rate = 1/(no-leak time) − 1/(with-leak time). Invert to get empty time.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Pipes A (fills in 6 hrs), B (fills in 9 hrs), and C (empties in 18 hrs) are opened in rotation: A runs 1st hour, B the 2nd, C the 3rd, repeating. Starting from empty, how long to fill the tank?
questions.explanation:
Per 3-hr cycle: 1/6+1/9−1/18 = 3/18+2/18−1/18 = 4/18 = 2/9.
After 4 complete cycles (12 hrs): filled = 4×2/9 = 8/9. Remaining = 1/9.
In hr 13 (A runs at 1/6 per hr): time to fill 1/9 = (1/9)÷(1/6) = 6/9 = 2/3 hr = 40 min.
Total = 12 hrs 40 min.

**Short Trick:** Cycles fill in integers; handle fractional remainder in the next partial hour.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
